On a 9 or lower, the weapon shatters and destroys the weapon, releasing a biting burst of cold that deals 2d6 cold damage to all creatures within 10 feet of the weapon. After 7 days, a coldfire weapon loses the enchantment and becomes nonmagical again. Once the anvil has been used to enchant a weapon in this way, it can't do so again for 1d6 + 1 days.

rows.D35: This ring grows and shrinks to fit its wearer, but always seems slightly large for the finger it's on. The ring has an extradimensional space inside it dedicated to carrying armor. You can magically bind one set of unworn light, medium, or heavy armor to this extradimensional space over the course of 1 hour by resting the ring on top of the armor. Only one suit of armor can be bound to the ring's extradimensional space. Binding a second suit breaks the bond with the first one, causing it to be forced from the extradimensional space and appear in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the ring. While wearing the ring, you're considered to be within 100 feet of any armor stored inside its extradimensional space. While wearing this ring, you can use an action to speak its command word and touch a suit of bound armor, even if you're wearing it, to shunt it into the ring's extradimensional space. Speaking the command word again while the armor is in this extradimensional space causes you to magically don the armor, adjusting to fit you as needed, or causes it to appear at your feet (your choice). If you're already wearing a suit of armor when you don one in this way, the bound armor appears at your feet instead. If the armor would magically prevent you from doffing it, this property of the ring has no effect. You can create an instantaneous, harmless sensory effect when you don or doff a suit of armor with the ring in this way, such as a shower of sparks, a puff of wind, faint musical notes, or an odd odor. When found, the ring has a 50 percent chance to have a set of bound armor in its extradimensional space. The GM can choose a suit of bound armor from the following table or roll a d12 to determine it randomly. d12 Armor 1 Padded 2 Leather 3 Studded leather 4 Hide 5 Chain shirt 6 Scale mail 7 Breastplate 8 Half plate 9 Ring mail 10 Chain mail 11 Splint 12 Plate

rows.A36: Blackthorn Spear of the Moonless Hunter
rows.D36: This spiny, black bone spear is a favorite among nocturnal hunting tribes. While attuned to the spear, you can always see the faint outline of it, even in total darkness. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. This spear contains a fragment of the moonless hunter, an ancient spirit that can be channeled to assume some of its powers. While you're not channeling the spirit, you can use a bonus action while holding this spear to call forth the magic within it and assume the spirit of the moonless hunter. While you're assuming this spirit, your eyes become pure white, and you gain the following benefits: You ignore the effects of exhaustion. You can't sleep or be put to sleep by magical means, and you can't take or benefit from finishing a long rest. You have advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks and on Wisdom (Perception) and Wisdom (Survival) checks made to detect and track creatures. You can see normally in darkness, both magical and nonmagical, out to a range of 120 feet. Your attacks with the blackthorn spear of the moonless hunter deal an extra 1d6 necrotic damage to any creature it hits. Your movement speed increases by 5 feet. You can assume the spirit in this way for up to 8 hours or until you release it as a bonus action. The effect ends early if you are more than 120 feet away from the blackthorn spear of the moonless hunter for more than 1 minute. When the effect ends and you are no longer assuming the spirit of the moonless hunter, you gain 2 levels of exhaustion as the spirit returns to the spear. Exhaustion gained in this way can only be reduced by finishing a long rest.

rows.D37: You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. The war pick deals an extra 1d4 fire damage to any target it hits. This weapon has 4 charges and regains 1d4 expended charges each day at dawn. When you hit a target that is either made of metal or wearing metal armor, you can expend 1 charge to inflict an extra 2d8 fire damage to the target.

rows.D38: You gain +1 bonus to attack and damge rolls made with this magic weapon. When you make a thrown (20/60) attack with this weapon and your attack roll beats the target's AC, as bonus action, you may choose to teleport to it upon impact, gripping the weapon. This also works with inanimate objects.

rows.D39: Damage 1d6 Slashing by blade or 1d6 by crossbow (30/90). As an action you can strike a special chord on the warlute. One creature of your choice has advantage on their next roll. You can not use this feature on yourself and a creature can be affected  by it once per long rest. You can use this feature number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minum is one). You regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. Whenever you grant someone Bardic Inspiration, the die recieves +1 bonus. If you inspire an ally in the same turn asyou make a successful weapon attack against a creature using this lute, inspiration die recieves a +2 bonus instead.

rows.D40: While worn, 1d4 times a day it gives you advantage on stealth and nature checks. By wearing this ring, you are also able to speak with wolves.

rows.D41: Frequently abused in academic circles, these fragile masks endow the wearer with the ability to form perfect memories - everything the wearer sees, hears, thinks and does while wearing the mask is permanently etched into their mind. Anyone who can see or hear the wearer is similarly affected with permanent memories of the wearer's actions. These secondary users do not form perfect memories of anything that does not involve the individual wearing the mask.

rows.D42: Its origins unknown, this orb has the word, "Passage" inscribed in various languages throughout it. It's gold lining holds arcane infused onyx that slightly dims any light within 5ft. of it. To activate this orb, you must place a key upon its center axis and speak words "Find a Passage". When the orb is activated, the key is dissolved into the orb. The orb then floats at your side and begins to lead you, on your command, to the lock the dissolved key was made to unlock. If the orb is within 5ft. of the lock, it is magically unlocked. Once the orb has unlocked 3 locks, the orb dissolves.

rows.D43: A ring that smells of rich cinnamon and sweet fruit, creating a unique scent that encapsulates the wearer, confusing creatures that rely on scent. As a bonus action, the wearer of the ring can conjure a ghostly pie and attempt to smash it in the face of a creature within melee range (improvised weapon attack). On a hit, the pie explodes in the creature's face, blinding them for one turn and dealing 1d4 force damage. If the attack misses and there's a creature directly behind the original target, another attack is made against this new target (target has +1 to his AC). The Ring of Splat contains five charges and regains 1d4+1 charges every day at dawn. Ghost pie can only be eaten by ghosts.

rows.D44: The Chalk of Hiding makes a creature or item on a flat surface disappear when a complete border is drawn around it. From the outside, the surface will appear completly normal. The Chalk of Hiding can last up to several years in the right conditions or until the border is broken. If a body part exits the border, it will become visible. The Chalk of Hiding can draw for 50 feet. Chalk of Hiding does not disguise sound or smell.

rows.D45: This mace is made out of various books stiched together. You gain proficiency in using a mace while weilding this weapon if your class is wizard and use your intelligence ability score for what would regularly be strenght. If your intelligence is higher than 15 you gain an additional +2 to attacks and an additional +4 to damage. Half of the damage dealt is psychic if the creature has an intelligence score of 12 or less.

rows.D46: This +1 Greatclub does 1d10 bludgeoning damage and has 3 charges. When you fail a Charisma (Persuasion) or Charisma (Intimidation) check against a target you may use your reaction and expend a charge to make an attack against the same target with the greatclub. If the attack hits, you may immediately make another Charisma check of the same type against the target at advantage, as a bonk to the head forces them to reconsider your proposition. Furthermore, the target does not become hostile for having been hit on the head with the club, unless it was already hostile. The club regains one charge each dawn, as long as it was used in combat the previous day.

rows.D47: This energy +1 longsword was designed to attack directly through the enemies exoskeletons and armor. It inflicts damage to the mind instead of the body and allows to best much larger and resilient foes in the hands of an expert user. The sword has a total of 6 charges. It regains 1d4 charges every day at midnight. As a bonus action you can expend two charges to ignore 2 AC of any creature with non magical armor you hit this tun. As an action you can expend 1 charge to detect any illusion or invisible creature within 20 feet radius around the sword.

rows.D48: A ring carefully carved from a single stone. It feels surprisingly heavy until worn. This ring has 6 charges for the following other properties: as a reaction to taking damage from a melee or ranged weapon attack, you can expend 1 charge to gain the effects of stoneskin, including against the triggering attack, until the end of your next turn ; as a bonus action you can expend 2 or more charges to becoem immune to all damage until the end of your next turn, during which time you are also considered petrified. You can increase the duration of this effect by one round for each additional charge you expend beyond the second. The ring regains all expended charges daily at dawn.

rows.D49: A small drinking glass made of unicorn ivory. It has the power to detect and instantly neutralize any kind of poison, toxin or venom that's poured into it, wether natural or alchemically created and turn it into clear, drinkable water. If any liquid poured into it contains poisonous elements, they will also be neutralized and the poured liquid will remain.

rows.D50: Loved by jerks and many bards, this sword keeps swearing to demotivate his enemies. It's magical +1 shortsword. The sword is sentient and has following stats: INT 6 (-2); WIS 6 (-2); CHA 16 (+3). Its alignment is chaotic stupid. After hitting an enemy with this sword, enemy must succeed a WIS saving throw against DC 13. If enemy fails, he gets insulted by the sword and recieved 1d4 psychic damage. The insults are mostly random and stupid.

rows.D51: A dagger which gives advantage when attacking a creature from the inside. It also contains a vial of poison in the hilt that can cause a creature to vomit on a failed DC 15 CON save.

rows.D52: This +2 warhammer is made from the reinforced tooth of a giant!

rows.D53: You can use this tome once a day. This tome appear to contain spells: message, mage armor, hold person, speak with dead, ice storm, teleport, wish. When one of these is cast, the DM reveals the spell's true nature: message = massage: 120 ft, the target recieves a pleasant backrub; mage armor = mage armoir: summons a fancy wardrobe; hold person = fold person: target must succeed a wisdom save or bend over backwards and be restrained for 1 round; speak with dead = speak with dad: for 1 minute you can communicate aloud with your father, this fails if they are dead or on another plane; ice storm = ick storm: gross sludge rains down for 1 minute, creating difficult teraain in a 20ft radius; teleport = telepoot: creates a small fart noise within 60 ft; wish = wash: a wet sponge cleans you vigorously for 1 minute

rows.D54: Wearing these player has advantage to arcana and history knowledge checks. The wearer of these spectacles can read books three times faster than normal. Once per day you can comprehend languages (reading only)

rows.D55: This double bladed dagger can be struck on a surface and made to ring like a tuning fork. When target is cut with it, they will only be able to hear a loud ringing sound in their ears, effectively becoming deaf for 5 minutes.

rows.D56: This is +1 magical whip. Whenever you deal damage to a creature with this magic weapon, several petals are dispatched into the creature's space in a 5ft cube. After one second the petals explode, dealing 1d4 fire damage to all creatures in the area. You can cas the Firebolt cantrip. The spell manifests as petals which explode upon contact. You can use this feature three times a day.

rows.D57: As an action you can plant this staff firmly in the ground and speak a command word. Over the course of 1 minute, the staff grows into a large tree with a tree house in it. When the tree is fully grown a rope ladder drops from the tree house. The tree house is 40 ft. from the ground. The outer dimensions of the treehouse are 10ft by 10ft. However, the single room on the inside is 30ft by 30ft. The tree and its house last indefinitely or until you spend another action to speakthe command word again. The tree only reverts back to staff (over the course of one minute) if no creatures are inside the tree house. If the tree is destroyed the staff is destroyed as well.

rows.D58: When eaten, this cupcake provides enough nourishment to sustain a medium sized creature for 3 days. The creature does not feel bloated, and can still eat while affected by the cupcake. This cupcake is treated as a fey creature for the purposes of detecting creature types.

rows.D59: You're attacked, but in your pocket is the most tactical weapon any fighter could ask for: sand. It's coarse and rough and irritating and it gets everywhere. This non-dimensional pouch can be slapped onto any article of clothing to create a pocket that's always filled with sand. There's always enough sand for a perfect handful. Tipping the pocket over does nothing. Sand must be removed via a hand, paw, talon or an equivalent. As a bonus action, you can throw pocket sand into eyes of a creature within five feet of you. The creature must have eyes for the Sand of The Pocket to take effect. When the sand is thrown, both parties make contesting dexterity rolls. If the thrower is successful, the Sand of The Pocket enters the creature's eyes and that creature has disadvantage on any attacks and ability checks they make that require sight for one round. The Sand of The Pocket is also ideal for sandcastles.

rows.D60:
This is no ordinary fork... but it is shiny. As soon as you saw it, you knew you had to have it!
You have a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
This fork purifies any food it comes into contact with.
The fork seemingly stores all the nastiness from the food it purifies. Once per day you can take a -5 to your attack roll and deal an additional 5d10 poison damage to a creature you hit (releasing the nastiness).
Proficiency with a dagger allows you to add your proficiency bonus to the attack roll for any attack you make with it.

rows.D61: For 1 hour after drinking this delicious ale crafted by the dwarves of Ironforge Brewing Company, you gain 10 temporary hit points that last for 1 hour. For the same duration, you are under the effect of the bless spell (no concentration required). This golden potion bubbles and steams as if boiling.

rows.D62:
This worn brass door knob has a dimly glowing letter C on its circular face.
Holding the door knob in the air, as if holding one belonging to a real door, a shimmering door projects in the direction the knob is pointing. Turning the handle and opening the door will reveal a cupboard with 10 shelves. At any one time, 5 shelves can be seen, only being moved by use of a pulley found inside the cupboard.
Each shelf is 4 feet wide, 1.5 feet deep, and has 2 feet of free space above it. A shelf's weight capacity is 100lb's and exceeding this will cause the shelf to disappear, tossing the contents of the shelf on to the floor. Breathing creatures inside the knob can survive up to a number of minutes equal to 10 divided by the number of creatures (minimum 1 minute), after which time they begin to suffocate.
If the Brass Knob is attached to a wall, or a real door, it is inert until removed.
Placing a Brass (Door) Knob inside an extradimensional space created by a bag of holding, portable hole, or similar item instantly destroys both items and opens a gate to the Astral Plane. The gate originates where the one item was placed inside the other. Any creature within 10 feet of the gate is sucked through it to a random location on the Astral Plane. The gate then closes. The gate is one-way only and can't be reopened.

rows.D63:
This wand has 4 charges. While holding it, you can use a reaction to expend 1 or more of its charges to cast the Counterspell spell from it. For 1 charge, you cast the 3rd-level version of the spell. You can increase the spell slot level by one for each additional charge you expend.
The wand regains 1d4 expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the wand's last charge, roll a d20. On a 1, the wand crumbles into ashes and is destroyed.

rows.D64:
The Bow of Thorns is a dark-wood bow decorated in silver and green. Despite its wicked-looking silver thorns, the bow does not cut its bearer.

While wielding this longbow, you have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls. The bow has 3 charges. As a bonus action, you may expend one of these charges to cast Hail of Thorns or Ensnaring Strike. The bow regains 1d4-1 charges at dawn.

rows.D65: The head of this greataxe is made of the finest silver and hilt is made from ancient bark from north, which has been infused with cold magic for centuries. It was specifically used to slow down the undead hordes from attacking the villages. This gretaxe adds +1 to attack and damage rolls. When attuned to this greataxe, before attacking you can use 1 of its 2 charges to deal extra 1d8 cold damage if you hit the target. If you hit the target, the target has to make DC 8+prof+your STR modifier CON save, if the target fails, his speed is halved till your next turn. Undead has disadvantage on this save. If you miss the target, you still roll 1d8, and the cold damage gets dealt to you(which is halved) and you also need to make DC (8+ your STR modifier)/2 CON save, to see if you will not get slowed till your next turn.

rows.D66: This sleek spear with a gold shimmer, like the sunrise in waves with blueish green watery tether behind it. The spear can be thrown to enemies, ignoring cover, but dealing 1/2 damage, if the enemy is behind 1/2 cover; 1/4 damage if the enemy is behind 3/4 cover and behind full cover, the spear will deal 1 damage. Cover can't be more than 5 feet wide. If the target is hit, it has to make DC 8+prof+STR  STR save. If the target fails, it's grappled. The grappled target, you can pull to yourself with bonus action by 5 x STR modifier feet. If the target is behind cover, it's pulled into it and the damage from cover is 1d4+STR modifier for 1/2 cover; 1d4+2+STR modifier for 3/4 cover and 2d4+2+STR modifier for full cover.

rows.D67: While creature is attuned to and in posession of this item they recieve the following benefits: They always roll a 15 when determining initiative. Their age may not be altered through unnatural means. They are immune to effects of the Slow, Haste, and Time Stop spells.

rows.D68: Using an action to read this dark scroll causes horrifying memories, fears, and regrets to violently invade the minds of up to 10 creatures of your choice that you can see within 60 feet of you. Each creature must take DC 15 Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 5d10 psychic damage and becomes frightened of you for 1 minute or until it takes damage. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage and isn't frightened. Non-sentient creatures are immune.

rows.D69: The Amulet of Cheetah Speed improves the movement of the wearer of the amulet by 10 feet and allows them to use it once per long rest to cast Haste upon themselves.

rows.D70: The Belt of Antipode gives immunity to cold, but doubles the damage received from fire-based attacks.

rows.D71: When worn you can see and read magic as if you were under the effect of the detect magic spell. When removed, you are blinded for a length of time equal to how long you wore the spectacles. This blindness can only be cured when glasses are worn again or with restoration spell.

rows.D72: Aibat fought harder and better than most. He took his defeat gracefully. Maul was made of dragonbone with blue crystals embued in it. This weapon gave +1 to attack and damage rolls and each time used, it dealt extra 1d4 cold damage  to nearby creatures within 5 feet.

rows.D73: This potion flask contains a single black eye, carefully preserved and infused by alchemy. For one hour after consuming it, you can see normally in darkness, both magical and non-magical, to a distance of 60 feet.

rows.D74: This armor has been masterfully woven from silk rope, and provides the same Armor Class as leather armor. You can use an action to speak its command word, causing the armor to unweave itself into 100 feet of rope. Speaking the command word a second time weaves the rope back into armor.

rows.D75: When attuned to this amulet, you are resistant to force damage and gain +3 bonus in Arcana. This amulet holds four charges. You can use one charge to cast one Cantrip from the Wizard spell list. The amulet regains 1d4 charges after you finish a long rest.

rows.D76: While wearing this ring, your body gains the ability to digest and gain nourishment from rocks.

rows.D2: This slim blade was forged using strange, unearthly metals from a meteorite. When you use an action to toss this magic dagger into the air, it orbits your body at a distance of 1d4 feet. Another creature can use an action to grasp the dagger to separate it from you, either by making a successful attack roll against AC 24 or a successful DC 24 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check. You can use an action to seize and either wield or stow the dagger. When you take the Attack action while the dagger is orbiting you, you can use a bonus action to cause the dagger to attack a target within 10 feet of you. The dagger uses your attack roll and ability score modifier to damage rolls. Immediately after the attack, the dagger returns to orbit you. In addition, the dagger creates a small gravitational field that wards off harm. While the dagger orbits you, when you are hit by a ranged weapon attack, the damage you take from the attack is reduced by 1d10 + 4. If the damage is reduced to 0, the missile slows to a stop without hitting you and falls to the ground at your feet.

rows.D3: This flexible bow is made from the chitinous legs of a phase spider and retains some of its ethereal properties. The bow has 5 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dawn. When you make a ranged attack roll with this magic bow, you can expend 1 of its charges to cause the arrow to slip partially into the Ethereal Plane. When you do, the target of the attack gains no benefit from cover, including total cover, as long as the cover isn't made of lead or more than 1 foot thick. If you hit, the target takes an extra 2d6 force damage. Any effect that blocks travel through the Ethereal Plane also blocks the arrow. Alternatively, you can speak the bow's command word as a bonus action to expend 3 of its charges and fire an arrow at a point you can see within the weapon's normal range. When the arrow hits a solid surface, you vanish from your location and reappear in an unoccupied space nearest to that point.

rows.D4: This ruffled cloak of dull feathers and down grants you the resilience and cunning of a ravenous vulture. When you move while wearing this cloak, small, tattered feathers drift from the cloak that vanish when they touch the ground. While wearing the cloak, your Constitution score increases by 2 to a maximum of 20, you have advantage on saving throws against disease and poison, and you have resistance against poison damage. In addition, while wearing the cloak, you can speak its command word as a bonus action to cause it to transform into a pair of sickly vulture wings for 1 minute. While the cloak is transformed, you gain a a flying speed of 60 feet, and when you hit a creature that's missing any of its hit points with a melee weapon attack, that creature takes an extra 1d6 necrotic damage. This property of the cloak can't be used again until the next dusk. Curse. This cloak is cursed, and becoming attuned to it extends the curse to you until you are targeted by the remove curse spell. As long as you remain cursed, you are unwilling to part with the cloak, keeping it worn at all times. The cloak gives you an insatiable hunger for flesh, and while traditional food can sustain you, you no longer enjoy the smell or taste of it. While cursed, whenever you reduce a creature within 5 feet of you to 0 hit points, you're forced to make a DC 13 Wisdom saving throw. If the creature is a construct, undead, or plant, you automatically succeed on this saving throw. On a failed save, you are overcome with the urge to tear into the creature's flesh and feast: sacrificing any additional movement, action, or bonus action you had left on your turn. You can repeat this saving throw at the start of each of your following turns, ending your need to feast on a success.

rows.D5: This item appears to be a sword hilt that has a small hole on either end of it. The hilt is made of clear quartz and contains an hourglass with sand inside it. Despite the holes on the hilt, the sand never seems to flow out of the hourglass. You can speak the hilt’s command word as a bonus action to cause it to form a thin blade of sand. The hourglass spills sand from the bottom of the hilt that circulates up and around to form the blade and guard of the rapier before returning to the hourglass again through the hole at the top. You can speak the hilt’s command word again as a bonus action to cause all the sand to return to the hourglass. While the blade is formed, you gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. While holding the hilt, you can use an action to cast either the haste or slow spell (save DC 16) from it. You have advantage on Constitution saving throws you make in order to maintain concentration on a spell cast in this way. Once a spell has been cast using the hilt, it can’t be used to cast that spell again until the next dawn. The sands in the hourglass move quickly while you concentrate on a haste spell cast in this way, or more slowly when you concentrate on a slow spell.

rows.D6: This singular lens lets you faintly see and command the flow of time around a target. The eyepiece has 5 charges and regains 1d4 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. While wearing the eyepiece, you can expend 1 charge as a reaction at the end of another creature's turn to speak either of the eyepiece's two command words to warp the flow of time around that creature. You must be able to see the target, and it must be within 60 feet of you. Past. If the target is willing, it is teleported back to the space it was at the beginning of its turn. If another creature or object is occupying the space, the target is teleported to nearest unoccupied space instead. An unwilling target must succeed on a DC 16 Charisma saving throw or be teleported in this way against its will. Future. If the target is willing, it can immediately choose to move again, up to half its speed, without provoking opportunity attacks. After a target moves in this way, its speed is halved until the end of its next turn.

rows.D7: You gain a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. The lance has 4 charges and regains 1d4 expended charges each day at dawn. You can expend 1 charge as an action to surround yourself with a flurry of wind that lasts for 1 minute. While surrounded by this wind, you can take the Disengage action using a bonus action. You can expend a second charge of the weapon (no action required) while surrounded by the wind to extend the effect to any mount you’re currently riding. If you dismount or are forced off your mount, the effect fades from it. The effect ends early if you fall unconscious or are no longer wielding the lance. In addition, you can use the lance to cast the thunderwave spell at 3rd level (save DC 16). Once this property of the lance has been used, it can’t be used again until the following dawn.

rows.D8: These two magical weapons are bound by a powerful force. Despite there being two weapons, you only need to attune to one of them to use their properties. While holding one of the weapons, you can use an action to determine the distance and direction of the other paired weapon as long as you're on the same plane of existence. If you attune to one of the weapons while another creature is attuned to the other, you are each aware of the other creature's attunement and must make an Intelligence (Arcana) check contested by the other creature's Intelligence (Arcana) check. The creature that wins the contest remains attuned to the item, and for the next 24 hours, its attunement cannot be broken by another creature attempting to attune to the other weapon. The creature that loses the contest is no longer attuned to the weapon. While holding both weapons in either hand, you gain several benefits: You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with these magic weapons. Your perception of time is slightly quickened: allowing you to dodge attacks that would have normally hit you. You gain a +1 bonus to AC. When you roll a 20 on an attack roll using Hour (the dagger) against a creature, that creature is under the effects of the slow spell until the end of your next turn. When you roll a 20 on an attack roll using Minute (the shortsword), you're under the effects of the haste spell until the start of your next turn. When the effect ends, you don't suffer the normal effects of the spell ending. In addition, you can use an action to lay the two weapons down on the ground. When you do, they magically point north before spinning around to align and tell the current time. When they do, 12:00 is always facing north.

rows.D9: This gilded bow creates hazy illusions of the cosmos when drawn. Attacks made with this magic bow deal an extra 1d4 force damage to any target hit by it. When you see a creature casting a spell within 60 feet of you while holding this bow, you can use your reaction to draw from your own life force and attempt to counter it. When you do, you lose 30 hit points and fire a magical arrow of pure force from the bow toward the creature. If the creature is casting a spell of 5th level or lower, its spell fails and has no effect. In addition, the target must make a DC 16 saving throw, using its spellcasting modifier. On a failed save, the creature takes 30 force damage as the magic is ripped from them. On a successful save, the creature takes half as much force damage. Once this property has been used, it can't be used again until you finish a short or long rest.

rows.D10: These bracers can summon another pair of spectral arms below your existing ones. These arms can be summoned as an action and last for up to 1 minute before disappearing. While active, you can use the arms to manipulate an object, open an unlocked door or container, stow or retrieve an item from an open container, or pour the contents out of a vial. Each arm can carry up to 10 pounds. The arms stay attached to your torso at all times and cannot be moved to other parts of your body, but can be turned around to face the opposite direction. In addition, the gems adorning the bracers can amplify the arms’ strength for short bursts. The gems have a total of 5 charges and recharge 1d4+1 expended charges each day at dawn. By uttering the bracers’ command word using a bonus action and expending 1 charge, you can empower the arms to immediately make two unarmed melee attacks. The arms have a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls and use your proficiency bonus when making the attacks. Each strike does 1d4 magical bludgeoning damage upon a successful hit. Alternatively, you can expend 1 charge to double the arms’ carrying capacity and increase their duration to 5 minutes instead.

rows.D11: This magical platinum helmet has been blessed by a powerful, holy dragon. While wearing this helmet, you gain a +1 bonus to AC and saving throws, and when you use your breath weapon, you can choose to exhale a holy blue plume of healing energy instead. When you do, this breath weapon deals radiant damage, evil-aligned hostile creatures within the area have disadvantage on the saving throw, and any friendly creatures in the area regain a number of hit points equal to your breath weapon's damage dice instead. This property of the helm can't be used again until the next dawn.

rows.D12: This large, spiraling warhorn has 4 charges and regains 1d4 expended charges daily at dawn. You can use an action to expend 1 charge and blow the horn, summoning a war elk as if you had cast the find steed spell. A war elk uses the same statistics as a giant elk with the following changes: its size is Large, it has AC 14 (hide barding), and has 37 hit points. The steed disappears if your attunement to the horn ends. Alternatively, you can use an action to expend 1 of the horn's charges to speak its command word and then blow the horn. When you do, a spectral stampede of elk trample the area in a line 60 feet long and 15 feet wide that extends from you in a direction you choose. Each creature in the line must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes 4d10 force damage and is knocked prone. On a successful save, a creature takes half as much damage and isn't knocked prone. When you blow the horn, it emits a deep, rumbling tone that is audible 300 feet away.

rows.D13: This magical key is one of several made by a secret order of historians and archivists. While holding the key, you can use an action to twist the key, as if you were unlocking a door. When you do, a magical, spectral door slowly appears in front of you over the course of 1 minute, duplicating the effect of the magnificent mansion spell with the following change. The dwelling always includes a large library that magically includes copies of books, scrolls, maps, and more. The library does not count toward the total amount of space created by the spell. Its contents are strangely organized and seemingly change each time the key is used. A creature can visit the library and attempt to uncover a piece of knowledge, such as ancient poetry, the history of a forgotten kingdom, or the family lineage of a tyrannical king. The GM determines the checks and DCs needed to locate a given piece of information. For example, a book of foreign nursery rhymes may be easy to find, but a copy of necromantic research documents would be extremely difficult, if not impossible. When the spell ends, the key can't be used this way again for 24 hours.

rows.D14: This greataxe has +2 bonus to attacks and each hit deals additional 1d4 cold damage. Once per day you can use 1 charge of Howl of Winter, which as an action causes the axe to emit a chilling howl, freezing the air around you. All creatures within 15ft radius suffer 1d6 cold damage and must succeed on a strenght save DC 16. On a fail, they become paralysed in a pillar of ice for 1 minute. At the end of each of its turns, a frozen target can make another strenght save ending the effect on a success. Attacking the frozen creatures ends the paralysis effect and deals additional 1d6 cold damage.

rows.D15:
This crossbow is equipped with the latest in Gnome engineering, including a fitted looking glass to target your enemies and a series of levers and pulleys to help load and reload, though the working of which are a maze of steel and string. This weapon scores a critical hit on a 19 or a 20. Additionally, when a ranged attack with this crossbow misses, the player can still roll damage die – dealing damage equal to half of the number rolled with no modifier.
When this crossbow must be loaded roll a d6, on a 6 the player can ignore the loading property for this turn. On a success the player can make a DC16 perception to check to see if they better understand the working of how to load the crossbow, on a pass the next time a d6 roll is made to load the crossbow – the loading property is ignored by a 5 or a 6. This effect can continue until the player has achieved a complete mastery of the workings of this crossbow, and can always ignore the loading property.

rows.D16: A massive sword that is able to be wielded fluidly despite its size and weight. Much like the kraken itself.  It draws its power from the domain of the kraken. While within 15ft. of a pool of water it glows in a blue-green color and casts dim light in this color out to 10 ft. The weilder while holding the sword gains a swim speed of 30ft., and can breathe underwater. Additionaly, once per long rest the weilder can cast Wall of Water.

rows.D17: This cloak is made of the hide of an owlbear and has been infused with fey wild magic. The arms of the cloak can be used to draw or stow a weapon or item as a bonus action regardless of the size of the item and regardless of what type of container the item is stowed in. This does not superceed locked containers and the container must be within 5 feet of the user of this cloak. The cloak can hold, but not use or manipulate items. So long as the cloak has one free hand, it can make a melee attack as a bonus action. Attack +7 to hit, reach 5ft., one target. Hit 1d8+5 magical damage

rows.D18: While wearing this ring, you regain 1d6 Hit Points every 10 minutes, provided that you have atleast 1 hit point. If you lose a body part, the ring causes the missing part to regrow to full functionality after 1d6+1 days if you have at least 1 hit point the whole time.

rows.D19: The ring can hold 6 charges. You gain 1 charge whenever you kill (or actively assist in the killing of) a creature. As a bonus action you can activate one of the effects by spending charges. The effects are: (1 charge) You surrond yourself in an ominous aura that grants you advantage on Intimidation checks for 1 hour ; (2 charges) cloaks your body in darkness, grants +1 to your AC and you gain advantage on all Stealth checks; (6 charges) Imbues your next 3 melee and or ranged weapon attacks within 10 minutes with 3d6 Necrotic Damage. Curse : If there is one charge in the ring and you take a long rest, make a Wisdom saving throw (DC 14). On a failure you do not gain the benefits of the rest as your dreams are filled with the visions of the souls. THe DC increases by one for every extra charge the ring has.

rows.D20: This is +2 Spear. When you successfully hit a creature with this weapon, you can speak a command word which invokes the essence of desert sun as part of your attack. The creature has to make a Constitution saving throw (DC 14). On a failed save they take 2d4+2 Radiant damage and are blinded until the end of their next turn. On a successful save they take no damage. You can use this feature twice per day. After making a successful ranged attack against a creature with this spear you can instantly teleport to its location. This is a free action that is part of the attack and can be used once per round.

rows.D21: The crucibow is magical hand crossbow which blesses stakes fired from it with radiant damage. When loaded with a silvered dart it deals another 1d6 piercing damage, or if the target is undead another 2d6 radiant damage.

rows.D22: It is +2 armor. Your armor constantly secretes a thin layer of slime. Whilst wearing it you gain: resistance to slashing damage; vulnerable to bludgeoning damage; advantage on saves against being grappled. 3 times in a day you can, as an action, you and your equipment become gooey amorphous slime for 1 minute, or until you drop to 0 hitpoints, you cannot use any equipment or cast spells, however you gain advantage when grappling, while in this form, you can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide.

rows.D23: While wearing this ring, you have a deep understanding of yourself. You have advantage on Insight checks against yourself.

rows.D24: This arrow has tiny wings in place of fletching and when it is fired from a bow or thrown, it homes in on its target (+3 to hit)

rows.D25: This dart deals additonal +3 Force damage. As you throw this dart it seems to become alive and fly on its own. You recieve a +3 bonus on ranged weapon attack rolls made with this weapon. Because it flies on its own, it ignores both half-cover and three-quarters cover. As part of your attack, you can make the dart fly back to your empty hand. You can call the bird back to you from up to 200ft. Every time you deal damage to creature with this weapon you heal 1 hitpoint. When you critical hit a creature you heal 2 points instead.

rows.D26: A creature can use its action to drink this potion. A creature that drinks this potion is cured of any disease. This potion has no effect on constructs. If the creature is undead, this potion deals 5 radiant damage instead. If the creature is not a construct or undead, for next 48 hours it has advantage on Constitution saving throws, and any damage it deals from spells becomes radiant damage.

rows.D27: The stench of this thick brown liquid rivals the armpits of the most vile orc in the tribe. After drinking this potion you gain the following effects for 8 hours: all  damage spells you successfully cast deal double damage; everytime you cast a spell roll 2d20 outside the attack roll. If either d20 roll is a 1 or 2 the spell does not cast. Instead roll on the wild magic table.

rows.D28: When you drink this effervescent yellow potion your stomach and intestines gurgle and cramp.  After 1 hour you lay 3d4 eggs, each of which hatches soon thereafter producing an adorable fluffy chicken.  The chickens are loyal to you and follow you around where ever you go.  You maintain a rudimentary empathetic link to the chickens, and can instruct them to wait, follow, or to go to a place you can point at.  However these and any more complex commands are hindered by the fact that they are chickens.  A chicken can be thrown (range 30/60) dealing 1d4 chicken damage on a hit, tho the chicken becomes most upset with you.  A chicken can be eaten to regain hit points, but why would you do that, you monster!  If kept happy and well cared for, each chicken will lay 1 egg at dawn.  These eggs are delicious and eating one restores one spent hit die to the character who eats it.

rows.D29:
A clear glass bottle in the shape of a human skull. It is filled with a black fluid with shimmering red wisps moving through it. The bottle is magically sealed. While the magic is active, it requires a DC20 strength check in order to open the cork or to smash it open. Removing the magic makes the bottle function like a normal one. A tag on the bottle, written in Common, reads:

"Milking the evil out of a creature is not something I would ever like to do again.

You have no idea what I went through to make this.

Please handle with care. This shouldn't need to be said, but DO NOT DRINK! I mean it. Do not even try to open it."

- Master Ranger Danion

When an evil aligned creature is within 30 feet of the bottle, the fluid inside starts to vibrate and emit a dim red light out to 10 feet.
If the bottle is opened, the fluid instantly expands to multiple times its original volume. From the fluid spawns 2d6 slithering trackers that are hostile to all creatures in the area that they can see.

rows.D30: While wearing this amulet, you can attune to one more item then normal.

rows.D31: This damascan steel circlet has light blue gem embed in it. While unattuned the circlet gives +1 to AC. When attuned you can speak 3 of its command words to light the gem. The gem can make three types of light sources, 20 feet blinding light - when creature is hit in 20 feet cone, the creature must make DC 15 CON save, if the creature fails, it's blinded for 1 turn, the same creature can't be blinded more than once and/or if the creature saved from it once, it can't be blinded again for next 24 hours; 60 feet light - makes 60 feet long cone as bright as daylight; 120 feet dim light - makes 120 feet long dim light cone.

rows.D32:
This seed has been dorment for millenia. It's hard to tell what it does or how it grows, but when you put it close to your ear, you are sure that you can hear some kind of tiny whispers. 
To activate it, in 3 day period you have to use atleast combined 40 levels of transmutation spells near it (in 5 feet radius from it). Druids can make Nature check, on DC 16, they know that they have to use transmutation spells for something, on DC 18, they know that they have to use 40 levels combined to make it grow into one of 4 plant types. On DC 22 they know what kind of plant they will grow - grasses, flowers, bushes, trees. Using speaking with plants spell, the DC gets lowered by 2. When aquired, GM or player rolls d12, to see what kind of plant he will get(player does not know). The plant is fully grown in 5 days, reagrdless of its type. Plants can be destroyed forever with fire, but after that they live like normal plants.
Grasses (They grow in 20x20 feet area):
1 - Flax. It was commonly cultivated for its fibers, which were also known as flax, as well as for its seeds. The fibers of this plant were commonly cultivated for use in textiles, being used to make linen. Elf wizards often wore sashes made from flax fibers that were woven into an intricate knotwork. Some were known to wrap flax fibers around the end of torches in place of cloth. The seeds of this plant could be pressed into a substance known as linseed oil. Wizards used flax seeds as a material component for the Enlarge spell.
2 - Blackroot. It was an herb that could be distilled to create a poison used in the Underdark. The herb caused paralyzation. One could be become immune to the poison by ingesting small quantities of it over a long period of time. Blackroot could be distilled into notoriously thick alcoholic blackroot beer. One tankard of it was considered to be almost a full meal.
3 - Mugwort. It was a common fast-growing weed often disliked by farmers and gardeners, but useful to druids and potion-makers. Mugwort plants often grew back within mere days after being cut. It is used tto brew a powerful anti-toxin called the Elixir of Silvanus - a powerful curative potion that could cure even the most lethal poisons. 
Flowers (They grow in 15x15 feet area): 
4 - Daisy. Daisy plants could be used to create healing poultices. 
5 - Powderpuff. It was a small white flower with bluish leaves that grew in the polar regions. It was a triple-stemmed plant with small bluish-green leaves. The flowers were white and small and highly poisonous. Any bruise caused the flowers to secrete a potent poison that could penetrate the skin and leave a creature in a catatonic state for ten days. The flowers could be dried and powdered to produce an explosive substance akin to smokepowder, but only about half as potent.
6 -  Selûne's Tear. It was a flower that grew in the Swamp on the Coast. It could function as a spell component when burned, allowing the summoning of a ghost. Summoned ghost is friendly to the creatures which used the transmutation to activate the seed. Selûne's Tears had green leaves and dark blue flowers. 
Bushes (They grow in 10x10 feet area):
7 - Blueberries. They were a common type of berry in the world that grew on bushes. Blueberries were one of the many types of edible berries in the world that could be used as material components for the spell goodberry. Some used blueberries in the treatment of certain medical conditions, such as dropsy and typhoid.
8 - Honeysuckle. The scent of these shrubs was one of many that saurials used to communicate emotions. The scent of honeysuckle expressed an emotion of tendernesss or concern. The petals of honeysuckles were commonly mixed with those of roses when making Lotus Cheese. Honeysuckles could be used to help treat liver, spleen, and respiratory disorders. Unicorns were fond of the taste of honeysuckles.
9 - Domesticated Forester's Bane. This plant was largely green to dark green. Its leaves were tough and broad, with sinewy ribs that radiated 5​ to ​7 feet from the bushy center. Within this center was three to six purple stalks with saw-toothed edges. Any leaves or stalks removed would regrow within two to eight weeks. Overall their bodies measured up to 15 feet in a radius. Whenever a creature stepped on or near the leaves of this plant, they would snap shut around them. The saw-toothed edges on the plant's stalks then gradually sawed away at the trapped prey. But because it's domesticated it will not attack the creatures which used the transmutation to activate the seed. 
Within the center of this bush grew large, plump berries that had a sweet smell to them. These berries were typically bright yellow, golden, greenish, or white. They were said to be very delicious and rich in protein.
Trees:
10 - Hiexel. Trees usually grew about 30 feet tall. They had sparse branches that curved to make an overall oval shape. They had silver-green bark. The wood itself was green. Hiexel produced a great quantity of smoke when burned, so it was useful in cooking and signal fires. Hiexel bark was used in bookbinding and as a sealant in buildings. The wood was unstable and so was not useful in construction or crafting.
11 - Phandar. Trees grew about 60 feet tall, had numerous curving branches sprouting from a knobby trunk. The branches faced away from the wind, meaning that a group of phandars almost always pointed the same direction. Phandar leaves were triangular and mottled green. Phandar trees were said to resemble ropers. Because of its strength, phandar wood was an excellent building material. It was also used in the crafting of bows, tools, and weapon handles. Its multicolored grains made it prized in jewelry making.
12 - Domesticated Gulthias tree. Gulthias tree grew about 50 feet tall and it was a plant infused with supernatural evil, capable of spreading corruption to nearby plant life and generating malevolent creatures known as blights. But, because it's domesticated, it can't corrupt nearby plant life, it still generates blights - first one right after the tree is grown, and then every 3 years new blight is born. They are friendly to creatures, which used the transmutation magic to make the seed activate. They are neutral to everyone else unless attacked or commanded to attack. They listen to simple commands of friendly creatures and try to complete them as best as they can. From Gulthias tree 1 of 4 blights can be born: Needle blight, Tree blight, Twig blight, Vine blight.

rows.D33: This was the weapon of Dominique Harl, a sightless paladin who frequently traveled Faerûn. When attacked, Dominique would unleash the black mist that is this halberd's namesake. This often gave him the advantage, for he lived in darkness all his life, seeing only with the inner light of faith. Dominique eventually fell, his body found in a dark forest, slain by a creature of the night even more at home in the shadows than he. It is a +3 Halberd (1d10+3) and deals piercing damage. To use it, you need strength of atleast 13 and to have atleast 1 level in Paladin. The weapon has 3 charges, spending one charge, around the weapon black mist appears in 10 feet sphere and its area is heavily obscured. It lasts for 1 minute and it can't be dispersed by strong wind or wind like abilities. It can be only dispersed at will by the wielder. You regain 1d3 charges after long rest.

rows.D34:
Gauntlets of Ogre Power: Hands of Takkok
The Hands of Takkok are exactly that: ogre's very hands. He lost them when he attacked a strange man crossing the Spine of the World. The mysterious man turned out to be a mage of incredible power, and he used Takkok's hands to create this pair of ogre skin gauntlets. These gauntlets set wearers strength to 19, if it's already 19 or more, gauntlets don't give any effect.

rows.D35: This serated dagger was used to brutally damage enemies and scare them off, when they see how brutal it is. It gives +2 to attack and damage rolls. If you attack a surprised creature, it is an automatic critical strike. If you kill the creature with a critical strike, all other creatures in 10 feet radius must make DC 15 constitution save. If failed, the creatures are feared for the next turn and they don't become immune to it after that, if succeeded, creatures don't get feared and are immune to this ability from this dagger for next 24 hours.

rows.D36: This flawless steel-bladed glaive is the archetype of all glaives, and all other glaives bow before it. It gives +1 to attack and damage rolls. When you deal damage with this weapon, no other glaive within your line of sight can deal an equal or greater amount of damage until the end of your next turn.

rows.D37: The pint is a drinking pint with a metal bottom and wooden rim. It is enchanted to fill with magical alcohol, coming from the metal bottom, and stopping at the wooden rim. This alcohol, if consumed as a bonus action, will trigger a 1st level barbarian's rage. It is not advised to consume this alcohol more than once in 1d6+1 days, but if consumed in that time period, character must make DC 15 Constitution save, if failed, character falls unconscious for 1d12 hours. The effect does not trigger to creatures who are immune and/or resistant to poison or disease and it tastes like simple beer.

rows.D38: This hammer was designed to shake the core of even the strongest structures. All of your melee attacks against large objects or structures deal double damage. Your melee attacks against creatures of the construct type deal an additional 1d8 weapon damage.

rows.D39: As an action you can blow in this flute, to play Crab RaveTM and it summons a swarm of crabs 30 feet from you. Swarm has 6d4 HP, AC of 11, speed of 20 feet and deals 1d6 damage. You can control swarm as a bonus action. Once you use this feature you can't use it till long rest and any summoned crabs dissapear.

rows.D40: This necklace is made of 5 runestones. Your runestones can absorb threatening attacks against you. Whenever you take damage from an attack, hazard, or spell, you can use a reaction to expend any number of runestones, rolling 1d6 per charged runestone. You subtract the total rolled from the damage inflicted by the attack, hazard, or spell. If you have 5 unused runestones, you emit bright light in a 5 foot radius and dim light for an additional 5 feet. After spending all your runestones on a long rest roll a d20, if it's 10 or below, runestones are inactive and you can try again in next long rest.

rows.D41: Wearing these glasses allows the user to see magical items as they truly are. The proper instructions to activate the object appear like floating words before the wearer of these glasses. The glasses may be used to cast identify three times per long rest.

rows.D42: The thick fluid of this potion is in constant motion, and eyes seem to appear and dissolve within it. After drinking it as an action, gibbering mouths appear across your body, and you gain a bites melee attack as bonus action which deals 2d6 piercing damage. The effect lasts for 1d4+1 rounds. If you kill a creature with your bites attack, it is absorbed into you, and you gain one of the creatures stats for remaining rounds (special abilites->resistances->speed->your lowest ability score->your highest ability score).

rows.D43: You can use an action to read this scroll, which causes it to fold itself into a suit of paper plate armor. The armor functions like normal plate armor in all ways and also gives 6d6 temporary hit points, but is destroyed after your temporary hitpoints are used.

rows.D44: Attuned creature can target as an action a nonliving source of heat within 60 feet of itself that it can see. Gloves then extinguishes up to 15 square feet cube of the source, gaining 5 temporary hit points for each 5 foot square affected. Also, if you have gained temporary hitpoints this way, you don't suffer from cold environment.

rows.A45: The Means of Destruction (Hammer and sickle)
rows.D45: Dual wielded hammer and sickle. All damage dealt by these weapons is divided equally among all hostile creatures within 20 ft of the target.

rows.D46: Thin the herd. This is +2 Halberd, which gives +2 to attack and damage rolls. Halberd has 3 charges. You can use one charge as reaction when someone has attacked your ally in 30 feet radius, to deal the same amount of damage splitted to two weakest enemies in 60 feet from you. When all charges are used, you regain charges after long rest.

rows.D47: When you drink this potion, you regain 5 sorcery points. If you use it when you have used less than 5 sorcery points, you still use the full potion, regaining your maximum sorcery points avaiable. If you are not an sorcerer, you don't gain any additional effects.

rows.D48: Blade is a dagger bestowed to the Knights by The Round Table. It's possible the blade has been passed down from generation to generation alike the Knight title. On blade there is an inscription in elven what says - "Release the souls of the faithful departed from the pains of the bottomless pit. Free them from the mouth of the lion, lest hell swallow them up, lest they fall into darkness. This, in iron, and pass over from death to life, the blood of the souls of his sacrifice to the salvation of the human souls to come." This dagger gives +2 to attack and damage rolls, and three times per long rest you can cast Enervation spell as 5th level spell.

rows.D49: An experimental (directed-energy) weapon, it fields a weaponized Lightning stone system that releases a focused stream of arcing lightning, which has devastating effect on the flesh of human. The Induction Lance can fire six shots before needing to be reloaded. It deals 1d12 lightning damage. You can spend 5 shots to shoot out a ball of lightning, which on impact deals extra 4d12 lighting damage in 10 feet sphere, creatures must make a DC 15 Dexterity save, to halve the damage. You can reload this rifle with bullets or electrum coins and reloading spends an action.

rows.D50: Gloves are a combination of adamantine and arcane technology and design. These pair of gloves are built and designed for the specific purpose of focusing and manifesting arcane energies that pass through the hands. On the hands of a arcane user it magnifies their powers. For a non-arcane user, it deals bigger damage to objects. When attuned to this item, your spells are casted 1 level higher, spending the current spell slot and unarmed melee attacks on objects always critically strike.

rows.D51: An eclectic art collector, Pierre l'Avenezars, is rumored to possess several of the Stones of Sympathy. Just what he plans to do with the stones is unknown. Stone of Sympathy radiates a permanent Sympathy (DC 18) effect that affects a certain race or subtype of creature, including intelligent creatures (DM's choice). Affected creatures need to make a DC 18 Wisdom Saving throw, on failed save creatures feel elated and pleased to be in the area or desire to touch or to possess the Stone. The compulsion to stay in the area of the stone or to touch it is overpowering.

rows.D52: With this rifle foe’s have no weak spots, even if they appear to have none. The damage dealt by this rifle ignores resistances and immunities. It has range of 100/300. It deals 3d10 piercing damage to large or smaller enemies. If target get's killed, the bullet travels further to it's maximum distance, if another enemy is hit, that enemy suffers 1d10 bludgeoning damage. If the first target is huge or larger, the 3d10 damage is bludgeoning instead and bullet shatters. Rifle has only 1 shot, and has to be reloaded as an action.

rows.D53: This weapon was made for strongest northern people. To wield it, you must have atleast Stength of 16 and Dexterity of 14. It's attributes are heavy, two-handed. It deals 1d10 damage as an attack, but you can make heavy swing attack spending an action, bonus action and half of your movement speed which deals 3d10 damage and target must make 8+STR+Prof Strength saving throw, if failed, target is knocked prone.

rows.D54: To attune to this item, you must be a construct. When attuned, your maximum intelligence increases by 2 and your intelligence score increases by 1.

rows.D55: Knight's Stamina: When attuned to this helmet you have resistance to Necrotic and Posion damage and are immune to being frightened. You gain a +1 bonus to your Constitution score every day up to a maximum of +4. Curse: Death's Call: Every day you wear this helmet you make a Wisdom saving throw (DC 12). The DC increases by 2 every day you wear this helmet. On a failed save you take 2d8 Psychic damage and you lose all COnstitution bonuses from this item. The following time you fail, the damage increases by 2d8, this effect stacks.

rows.D56: A crazy mage created this staff before he used up all his blood to cast his very last spell. With this staff you can cast spells without using spell slots. If you do so, you lose 1d10 HP per spell level after casting a spell.

rows.D57: A golden orb with 6 buttons on it. Depending on the order the buttons are pressed in, a different effect is produced by the orb. As an action, you can use it, roll 6d6, the most commonly rolled number determines the effect that the orb produces. 1. 200 gp appears in an adject square. 2. Fireball is cast in a random sqaure within 20 ft. 3. Polymorph is cast on a random creature within 20 feet. 4. A random magical potion is produced. 5. The orb summons 1d4 Flumphs. 6. An uncommon magic item is produced. 1,2,3,4,5,6. A homunculus is summoned. It is loyal to the person holding the orb. You can use the orb once per day.

rows.D58: A single shot firearm with a special function. Load one Platinum Piece into the chamber and whisper a type of coin. You may then make a ranged attack (60/100) against a target of your choice. On a hit the target takes an amount of force damage equal to the number of specified coins in their inventory.

rows.D59: This longsword is infused with deity's favor, which allows you to smite those who defy your agenda. This longsword gives +1 to attack and damage rolls. It gives +1 to your Charisma score. You can use Sneak Attack feature with this longsword. Once per long rest, you can cast wrathful smite spell. Spellcasting modifier is 8 + proficiency bonus + Charisma modifier

rows.D60: During attunement, this item is implanted into the base of your neck. While attuned, you are able to manipulate magical energies with your brainwaves and do not need material components for spells except for those with a cost that are consumed. At 10th level, your spells no longer need somatic components, and at 15th level they no longer need verbal components

rows.D61: This longsword deals 2d6 slashing damage, it has two-handed and finesse properties. The sword holds 3 charges, one charge can be used to cast Zephyr Strike as bonus action or Warding Wind as action.  You regain 1 charge per short rest and 3 charges per long rest. This weapon can also be used with sneak attacks.

rows.D62: While attuned to this circlet, you can steel your mind against effects that remove your mental agency. If you fail a saving throw to resist being charmed, frightened or stunned, you can choose to succeed instead. You can use this feature as many times as your Wisdom, Inteligence and Charisma modifier combined. Your charges regain after long rest.

rows.D63: While wielding this weapon, you can use an action to target up to four creatures within 60 feet that you can see. These targets must each succeed a constitution saving throw (DC 16). You deal necrotic damage equal to three times your character level, spread out equally among all targets that fail their save. If all targets succeed on their saving throw, no damage is dealt. You can choose to transfer the damage to your hit points, not exceeding your maximum amount or you can store it in this weapon and use it later till long rest. You can use this feature once per long rest.

rows.D64: This intricate gold headband is decorated with several small blue and deep purple gemstones. The headband grants the wearer bonus +2 to Intelligence score and increases by 2 Intelligence score maximum. You gain expertise in one of Intelligence based skills (arcana, history, investigation, nature, religion) and you always roll with advantage any Intelligence based skill (Including base Intelligence checks)

rows.D2: This black garnet amulet is carved into the shape of a bird's skull and is adorned with several dark feathers. At its center is a single phoenix feather that serves as a catalyst for this strange talisman's necrotic magic. While wearing this amulet, you are immune to necrotic damage. Shadow Form. When you are reduced to 0 hit points while wearing this amulet, a shadowy version of yourself rises from your unconscious body. You control this form, which has your equipment and statistics. It has 100 temporary hit points and resistance to all damage that isn't force, psychic, or radiant. The shadow form can't move more than 60 feet from your body. The shadow vanishes after 1 minute or when it falls to 0 temporary hit points. If the shadow survives for the duration, it returns to your body and causes you to regain a number of hit points equal to the shadow's remaining number of temporary hit points. If the shadow is defeated, the amulet is destroyed and you immediately fail 2 death saving throws. While your shadow form is defending you, your unconscious body is covered by an impenetrable veil of shadow. While covered in this way, you can't be interacted with: you are immune to all damage, don't make death saving throws, can’t regain hit points, and can’t be affected by spells or magical effects. A creature can use an action to make a DC 30 Strength check, moving the covered body up to 10 feet on a success. Once this property has been used, it can't be used again until 7 days have passed.

rows.D3: You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. When you use the glaive to reduce a Small or larger creature that is hostile toward you to 0 hit points, roll a d10. You gain temporary hit points equal to the number you roll. In addition, the glaive’s blade begins to glow with a sickly green haze whenever you gain temporary hit points in this way. While glowing, the first successful melee attack you make with the glaive deals extra necrotic damage equal to the number of temporary hit points you gained. Once you deal this bonus damage, the haze fades. The haze and any remaining temporary hit points are lost after 1 minute. Undead creatures killed by this weapon cannot be raised from the dead again. 6 feet under. The first time on your turn that you land a successful melee attack with this weapon against a creature that is prone, the weapon’s damage die is maximized.

rows.D4: This ancient stone axe hilt is intricately carved. At its center is a gap that houses a single, perfect diamond that's magically suspended in place and glows with an uncanny energy. While grasping the hilt, you can use a bonus action to cause a wide blade of pure prismatic light to radiate from the axe's head, or make the blade disappear. The axe's blade emits bright light in a 15-foot radius and dim light for an additional 15 feet. You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals force damage instead of slashing damage. When you hit an aberration or undead with it, that target takes an extra 1d12 radiant damage. While the blade persists, you can use a bonus action to expand or reduce its radius of bright and dim light by 5 feet each, to a maximum of 30 feet each or a minimum of 10 feet each. The light that comes from the diamond at the axe's center and forms the blade can be wrought to create powerful, destructive glyphs. Over the course of 1 minute, you can trace a glyph onto the surface of the axe, starting with the gem at its center, to recreate the effects of the symbol spell (save DC 17) with the following changes: The glyph you create as part of the spell exists on the axe and moves with it. The glyph can only be triggered when you hit a creature with the axe. The spell only affects the target that triggered the glyph. Aberrations and undead have disadvantage on the saving throw to resist the spell's effects. Once this property of the axe has been used, it can't be used again until 12 hours have passed. You can only have one glyph on the axe in this way at a time.

rows.D5: This weapon has a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magical weapon. The trident has a chain attached to its handle that can be used to retrieve the weapon once it’s been thrown using a bonus action. When you hit with a ranged attack using this weapon, it deals an additional 1d8 lightning damage. In addition, this trident acts as a conduit for the sky’s ferocious power. Immediately after hitting a creature with the trident, you can call down a bolt of lightning upon it, forcing it and all creatures within 5 feet to make a DC 16 Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, creatures take 6d10 lightning damage, or half as much on a success. Creatures have disadvantage on the saving throw if they’re submerged in water or wearing metal armor. You are immune to the lightning damage caused by this effect. This ability fails if the creatures are obstructed from the sky. Once you use this ability, you cannot do so again until the next dawn. Impale. You can use your action to try to impale and pull a creature toward you. If your target is a creature that is no more than one size larger than you, you can make a ranged weapon attack against it using the trident. If you hit, you can attempt to pull the impaled creature toward you by making a Strength (Athletics) check contested by the target’s Strength (Athletics) check. If you succeed, you can pull the creature up to 20 feet toward you.

rows.D6: This dark metal blade can slip between a person and their spirit to sever their connection to one another. You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, which deals slashing damage instead of piercing damage. While holding this weapon, you can use an action to cast the etherealness spell from it with the following changes: While on the Ethereal Plane, you can attack targets that you can see on the plane you originated from with the spirit cleaver. These attacks are made with advantage. If a target has 75 hit points or fewer after taking Sneak Attack damage in this way and isn't a construct or undead, it must succeed on a DC 17 Constitution saving throw or die. The spell has a duration of 1 minute, but ends early if you attack a creature on the plane you originated from with the spirit cleaver. Once this property of the weapon has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn.

rows.D7: This long-lost silver glaive once belonged to an elven king. Its impeccable elven make lets it be swung nimbly, despite its size. This weapon has the finesse property. In addition, you gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. Sentience. The glaive is a sentient weapon of chaotic good alignment, with an Intelligence of 14, a Wisdom of 15, and a Charisma of 16. It has hearing and darkvision out to a range of 120 feet. The weapon communicates telepathically with its wielder and can speak, read, and understand Elvish and Sylvan. Personality. The glaive is inhabited by the spirit of Kelren, the elven king of Imfe Mythse. His life's mission to rid his kingdom of demons, fiends, and other unwelcome ilk lives on inside the weapon. He seeks to rebalance the flow and seasons of nature, eager to destroy anything that threatens to change the natural ecosystems of the world. Kelren is stern, but honest. He may share stories of his kingdom from time to time if an anecdote serves to further his ambitions. A character who he deems unworthy of wielding the blade, such as a weak or evil creature, may be denied the ability to attune to the weapon. Elven Kinship. You are considered proficient with this weapon if you are an elf or half-elf. In addition, while attuned to this weapon, you have advantage on Charisma checks made to interact with fey creatures. Energy Nullification. If you hit a target with this weapon that is either resistant or immune to cold or fire damage, that target loses that resistance or immunity until the end of your next turn.

rows.D8: You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. This weapon can be attuned to by two friendly creatures together over the course of a long rest. If the weapon is attuned to by two creatures in this way, the weapon’s attack and damage bonus becomes +2 instead. This greatsword is made of two long scimitars that are held together by a powerful, unidentifiable magic. You can speak the weapon’s command word using a bonus action to separate it into a pair of scimitars or recombine them into the greatsword. If you are not already holding it when you speak the weapon’s command word and are on the same plane of existence as it, you can choose to summon either one or both scimitars to your hand as individual blades or as the combined greatsword. The scimitars have the thrown property with a normal range of 20 feet and a long range of 60 feet when separated. The scimitars deal piercing damage when thrown. Each scimitar also has its own elemental effect — either fire or cold — that inflicts an extra 1d6 fire or 1d6 cold damage with each strike, depending on which sword you hit with. When you hit with an attack using the greatsword, the target takes both fire and cold bonus damage from the attack. Each attuned creature can cast the fire shield spell once at 4th level without expending a spell slot. You do not need material or somatic components when casting it in this way. Once you cast this spell, you cannot cast it again until the following dawn.

rows.D9: This gold-trimmed book's cover is embossed with a portrait of Ogden Fellweaver, a legendary wizard infamous for his ill-gotten knowledge. If you can attune to this item, you can use it as a spellbook and an arcane focus. If your attunement to the book ends, anything written in the book disappears. Absorb Knowledge. Immediately after a creature that you can see within 60 feet of you casts a spell of 1st level or higher, you can use your reaction to make an Intelligence (Arcana) check. The DC equals 10 + the spell's level. On a success, the spell is magically added to the book in your own notation. You must be holding the book to use this property. If the added spell is a wizard spell and of a spell level you can prepare, you can prepare this spell just like your other spells. If the spell is not a wizard spell, its notation is garbled and impossible to use. Once this property has been used, it can't be used again until a number of days equal to the spell's level have passed. Shift Knowledge. While using this book as your spellbook, you can replace up to 3 spells from your prepared list of spells when you finish a short rest. Once this property has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn. Unknown Knowledge. While holding the book, you can use an action to channel its hidden knowledge. When you do, you gain proficiency in one skill or tool of your choice until the next dawn. If you're already proficient in the chosen skill or tool, your proficiency bonus is doubled, instead. Once this property has been used, it can't be used again until the next dawn. Curse. This book is cursed, and becoming attuned to it extends the curse to you. As long as you remain cursed, you are unwilling to part with the book, keeping it within reach at all times. In addition, you are compelled to use this book as your spellbook. Each time you prepare a spell from another spellbook, you take psychic damage equal to the spell's level.

rows.D10: This quiver has a lid with 5 holes in it and has depictions of the Elemental Planes on its side. It has 4 buttons along its top that correspond to each of the four elements: Air, Earth, Fire, and Water. Elemental Ammunition. The quiver can have up to 5 arrows or bolts on display at a time, which appear through the holes in its lid. You can press one of the quiver's buttons using a bonus action to cause it to create and display 1 elemental arrow or bolt. The type of arrow or bolt depends on the button you press. The quiver can produce up to 5 of each type of ammunition in this way each day. Any arrow or bolt created by this quiver is magical and has the following properties based on its element. The ammunition is only magical for you, and any arrow or bolt removed from the quiver loses its magic at the end of the turn. Air Ammunition. This ammunition is weightless and whistles softly as it moves. This piece of ammunition can be fired at its long range without disadvantage and deals an extra 1d6 thunder damage to any target it hits. In addition, any magical atmospheric effect that the arrow passes through cast at 3rd level or lower, such as a fog cloud or stinking cloud, is dispelled. Earth Ammunition. This ammunition carries an uncanny force behind it and turns to stone at its end. When you hit with a ranged attack using this ammunition, the target takes an extra 2d6 bludgeoning damage and must succeed on a DC 15 Strength saving throw or be pushed 10 feet away from you. Fire Ammunition. This ammunition has tongues of fire licking up its side and spews embers at the slightest movement. When shot, it erupts into a plume of white-hot flame. This piece of ammunition deals an extra 1d6 fire damage to any target it hits. Hit or miss, the ammunition explodes. The target and each creature within 5 feet of it must succeed on a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw or take 1d6 fire damage. Water Ammunition. This ammunition has a silky texture and glitters with watery reflections. A ranged attack made with this ammunition ignores the normal penalties of underwater fighting and deals an extra 2d6 piercing damage to any target it hits, or 3d6 piercing damage if the target is made of fire. In addition, any nonmagical flames within 10 feet of this ammunition's point of impact are extinguished when it hits. Paraelemental Ammuntion. You can press two compatible elemental buttons at the same time as a bonus action to create a paraelemental arrow or bolt: a hybrid piece of ammunition. Water and Air create Ice, Fire and Earth create Magma, Earth and Water create Ooze, and Air and Fire create Smoke. This ammunition appears from a special compartment in the quiver's lid. The quiver can create 1 of each type of paraelemental ammunition each day. A non-compatible combination, such as Fire and Water or Air and Earth, has no effect. Ice Ammunition. This special piece of frosted ammunition is cold to the touch and casts off snowflakes when it moves. When you hit with a ranged attack using this ammunition, the target takes an extra 3d6 cold damage and must make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the target is paralyzed for 1 minute. On a success, the target's speed is halved until the end of its next turn.
