A creature with resistance or immunity to cold damage automatically succeeds on the saving throw. A paralyzed target can make another Constitution saving throw at the end of each of its turns. On a success, the effect ends. The effect ends early if the paralyzed target takes fire damage. Magma Ammunition. This special piece of glimmering ammunition is warm to the touch and flakes off in sooty pieces. When you hit with a ranged attack using this ammunition, the target takes an extra 3d6 fire damage. Hit or miss, the area in a 20-foot sphere centered on the point of impact becomes unbearably hot until the end of the turn. Each creature within the area must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or gain 1 level of Exhaustion from the sudden flash of heat. A creature with resistance or immunity to fire damage automatically succeeds on the saving throw. Ooze Ammunition. This special piece of sticky ammunition gives off a faint, alchemical odor. This ammunition creates a unique grease spell (save DC 15) at the point of impact. This version of the spell covers a 20-foot square area, and any creature that starts its turn prone in the area takes 1d6 acid damage. Smoke Ammunition. This special piece of black ammunition feels smooth like coal to the touch and releases a faint wisp of smoke that quickly dissipates. This ammunition creates the effects of a unique fog cloud spell (2nd-level version) at the point of impact. This version of the spell is pitch black and heavily obscures the area.

rows.D11: At first glance, it appears as only the hilt of a greatsword. With a mental command of its wielder the sword will ignite in a brilliant flash of blue energy. The Void Blade is a +3 greatsword, that deals force damage in place of its normal slashing damage. The blade has 3 charges which replenish each dawn. Once you have damaged a creature with the blade, you can expend a charge. The target must make a Constitution saving throw. If they fail, you pick one of the following effects to take effect on them. A creature can have only one negative effect from this blade active on them at a time and they can remake their saving throws at the end of each of their turns. If they succeed, the effect ends. The DC for the Consitution saving throw is equal to 8+proficiency bonus+ your Strength modifier. Effects may be: the creatures loses ability to regain hit points for 1 minute; the target creature becomes blind for 1 minute; the target cannot cast spells until end of its next turn; you siphon the damage inflicted upon the target, healing yorself by the amount of force damage your attack did.

rows.D12:
This damascus blade was the pinnacle of a craftswoman's heart, a conduit of hope more powerful than dawn. However, consumed with the anguish of losing a loved one by their own hand, the original essence of the blade was tarnished by its creator. Discarded to the wayside, this beacon now struggles to find coexistence within the tides of darkness, less it be consumed by them...
- You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
- On a successful hit you add 1D6 Necrotic Damage to the roll
- Once per short rest you can have your blade ignore 3/4 Cover and Full Cover for an attack as the blade phases through any objects or allies in the way of your target. 
Similarly you can use this feature to instead shine a bright light within 5ft of the Wielder. All Creatures within this radius must succeed a DC 13 Constitution Saving Throw or be blinded until the start of their next turn. This secondary feature recharges every 1d4 Dawns. Proficiency with a longsword allows you to add your proficiency bonus to the attack roll for any attack you make with it.

rows.D13: This sword has an obsidian blade an the following properties. The sword is unnaturally heavy, requiring a Strenght ability score of 20 or higher in order to wield it. The first time you attack with the sword on each of your turns, you can add up to half of your Armor Class to the sword's attack and damage bonus, losing that amount of Armor Class until the start of your next turn. Whenever you use the sword to reduce a creature to 0 hit poins, its body turns into obsidian.

rows.D14: Add +2 to all Attack and Damage rolls made with this greatsword. As a bonus action you can slip into the shadows and reaapear in any aviable space within 30 ft. that you can see. When you reappear your physical form remains as an intangible shadow figure until your next turn. You can use this feature twice per long rest. You can cast Light cantrip at will while holding this sword. The target is always this sword and the light emits from the blade. This sword holds 3 charges. As an action you can expend these charges to cast spells from the list: (1 charge) Ray of Sickness; (2 charges) Darkness; (3 charges) Bestow Curse. The sword acts as a conduit and holds the concentration of these spells unless disarmed, dropped or the sword is sheathed. You can still only have one concentration spell active at a time. It regains charges after you finish a long rest. You use charisma as your spell cast modifier. Saving throws are a target of 15.

rows.D15: This 1 by 1 inch cube of stone is unnaturally perfect. It is exactly one inch in every dimension and its faces are perfectly smooth.

rows.D16:
You have a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

When an attuned archer of elven descent readies Ari'thalas, a silver arrow appears ready to be fired.  The arrows carry the enchantment of the bow and never need to be replenished.
The archer gains advantage on attack rolls against demons.
The archer’s eyes glow a bright silver when they aim the bow as the God of Archers touches them with his grace.  Their darkvision increases to 120 feet and can see through illusions within 120 feet. In addition the archer can detect evil auras and their strength within 120 feet.

rows.D17: The tear glows a bright white light. When you drink this tear outside of combat, you gain the benefits of a long rest. If you drink it while fighting, you instead gain the effects of the spells Heroism (using your highest ability modifier as your spellcasting ability modifier) and Haste for 1 minute (no concentration required).

rows.D18: Sir Eggbert is a sentient weapon that can do INT based checks and has +6 proficiency. It is +4 Greatsword, with 2d6 damage, and has advantage on attacks agains constructs and warforged.

rows.D19: A small item, easy to conceal, imbued with a dark magic, that awards its holder with coin as reward for the taking of a life. The forces behind magic are widely unknown, making it difficult to trace the origins of this strange accessory. Player must deliver the damage that kills creature. GP awarded = Creature's Challenge Rating x 2d6

rows.D20: When you apply the Googly Eyes of Sentience to any inanimate object or creation, it gains the capacity to feel, percieve, and experience subjectively. The creation survives, and perhaps, thrives, until both googly eyes are removed or their body destroyed. While some creations have ability to move, most do not. A mouth forms naturally and all creations speak one language of their creator's choosing. rows.D2: These leather bags have the stylized face of a griffon on their front and appear across the multiverse in strange locations. One may be found in the belly of a dragon, while another in the limbs of a great tree. Regardless of where it’s found, a Griffon’s Saddlebag is typically discovered by an adventurer with a destiny. The saddlebags are made by a great, six-armed griffon on the Astral Plane. Believed by some to be a demigod of pocket dimensions and craftsmen everywhere, the griffon is a patron of artificers and creators across the multiverse. The griffon creates magical items in its great forge using materials collected from various planes of existence to add to its collection. While no one knows exactly how to contact the griffon, it has a knack for knowing what items are needed by whom. Superior Holding. This 1-foot-wide bag always weighs 3 pounds, regardless of what’s inside it. It functions as a bag of holding that can only be pierced by another artifact. Placing a bag of holding, handy haversack, portable hole, or similar item inside the extradimensional space created by the saddlebag, or vice versa, destroys the extradimensional item but leaves the saddlebag unharmed. Any item stored within the other extradimensional space is magically moved to the space within the saddlebag instead. If doing so overloads the bag, random contents from either space are scattered in the Astral Plane. Magic Courier. At the GM’s discretion, the saddlebag’s beak opens up to reveal a letter. The magical script can be read by all creatures with an Intelligence score of 4 or higher. The note is a delivery request or similar that includes the name of an item as well as either specific or vague descriptions of a person or place. At the bottom of the letter is a price listed in coins or other form of payment, as well as a date or time depending on its urgency. If the saddlebag is brought to the described person or place within the allotted time, it dispenses the magical item into the hand of the appropriate recipient. If the payment isn’t received by the bag within 1 hour of dispensing the magic item, the item vanishes and is lost. After receiving the payment for an item in this way, the bag’s beak reopens to dispense a reward for the courier. Sell Magic Items. The saddlebag has a connection to the griffon’s forge on the Astral Plane. Depending on the magic item, you can sell a magic item to the saddlebag for half the cost of its base price. Spells. The saddlebag has 8 charges and regains 1d6 + 2 expended charges daily at dawn. While wearing the saddlebag, you can expend 1 or more of its charges to cast the following spells from it: detect magic (1 charge), identify (1 charge), or legend lore (5 charges). Additional Spells. At the GM’s discretion, such as after reaching certain milestones or completing Magic Courier quests, the saddlebag may offer the following additional spells that can be cast from it: blink (3 charges), dimension door (4 charges), divination (4 charges), etherealness (7 charges), fly (3 charges), magnificent mansion (7 charges), plane shift (7 charges), or secret chest (4 charges). Sentience. The saddlebag is a sentient chaotic neutral bag with an Intelligence of 13, a Wisdom of 15, and a Charisma of 16. It has hearing and normal vision out to a range of 60 feet. The bag can speak, read, and understand Common. When in the presence of only creatures it trusts, the bag’s beak moves when it speaks. Otherwise, the bag communicates telepathically with its wearer. The bag can speak and communicate with griffons. Personality. The bag’s purpose is to carry, collect, and deliver magic items. Different bags have different personalities, but they are for the most part largely pleasant to talk to. Their voices are bird-like and are filled with occasional coos and squawks, and their stitched eyes widen, squint, and move expressively. If the bag’s wearer or allies fail to fulfill Magic Courier quests, it may stop offering its magic to them. If it does, their items may be lost or inaccessible within the bag, or potentially spat out. While the bag provides the names of item recipients and delivery locations, it doesn’t know any more information than what was provided to it by the astral griffon. Regardless, it does its best to help its wearer and allies find the specified person or location on the letter. Destroying the Griffon’s Saddlebag. While there is no way to permanently destroy the saddlebag, piercing it with an artifact returns it to its place of origin for repair before it’s returned to the multiverse in a new location. Placing a Griffon’s Saddlebag inside the extradimensional space created by another Griffon’s Saddlebag returns both items to their place of origin and sends all the items stored within them to the griffon’s forge on the Astral Plane.

This extraordinary artifact was forged, in eons past, within the ever elusive walls of the Thane of Shadows. The Thane is a pocket Shadow dimension that, for a brief time, grants a select few admittance within its umbral walls as well as access to its priceless riches and knowledge. This immeasurable bounty has been accumulated by its countless previous visitors, who in return, must leave within the Thane, something within of great valuable to themselves. These select visitors are all beings who study, worship or are in some way tied to the essence of shadow.  This "path" to the Thane unfolds only when very specific conditions, astrological movements and chronological markers align. After this brief interlude, the connection expires and the Thane seals its entry once more, continuing on its march throughout the infinite planes of the multiverse.

At first glance, Gloom appears to be nothing more that a rune etched, leather wrapped adamantine handle befitting a long dagger, or even a short sword. A careless inspection may lead someone to disregard it as nothing more than an ornate handle with a shattered blade. In reality, the blade itself is a razor thin, physical manifestation of living shadow. This flat, two dimensional blade bleeds into existence from its adamantine handle with a mere thought from its attuned wielder. Once manifested, the blade continues to bleed shadow as it slices through most things with uncanny ease.

Dormant Attuned State:
The wielder gains a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls.
This blade deals an additional 1d4 cold damage, as the tendrils of darkness bleeding from the blade drain the warmth from the target.
Whenever a creature is struck with a Critical Hit, the target must make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw or become stunned until the end of the following round, (this is in addition to the Critical Hit damage). On a success, they are immune to being stunned by this effect for the next 24 hours.
Gloom's Umbral Embrace
In its fully awakened form, after prolonged attunement, (ex: a number of milestones/character levels decided by the player and DM, or reaching the next tier of play), the bond between Gloom's bleeding shadows and the darkness within the wielder becomes deeper and leads to a symbiotic relationship of sorts. The wielder is granted greater access to the items dark magics, and in exchange the artifact uses the wielder to feed on the darkness born from the demise of his foes. Gloom wants to be fed at all times, but the wielder's bond and partial mastery over the blade allows for a degree of control. The artifact's hunger can be held at bay for a number of days equal to the wielder's Intelligence modifier.  Every night, at the "witching hour", the wielder feels the darkness being drawn from him as the blade feeds on the energy from foes slain, recharging it's dark energies.

Exalted Gloom:
The attack and damage bonus increase to a +2 .
The blade's cold damage also increases to 1d6.
If struck with a Critical Hit, the target must now make a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or become stunned until the end of the following round. On a success, they are immune to being stunned by this effect for the next 24 hours.
Ridding the Shadows: When Gloom is thrown at a target, but before it hits, the wielder can choose to transmute his form and become one with the blade's shadows.
The wielder may then teleport along with Gloom and arrive instantly wherever the blade impacts, emerging adjacent to the target. If the attack misses the teleport fails and the blade's handle falls to the ground.  
Numbing Frost: The wielder may channel Gloom's frigid shadows, targeting enemies within range.
The wielder may fling an icy tendril of shadow to a target within 60 ft.
The tendril has the same propertied as a ray of frost.
This ability's damage increases based on the character's current level, (cold damage dealt is 1d8 at 1st, 2d8 at 5th, 3d8 at 11th, and 4d8 at 17th).
Numbing Frost may be a number of time equal to the wielder's proficiency modifier.
Gloom's Hunger: The blade's hunger must be sated. If the blade has not been fed within the allotted time, (this may be held at bay number of days equal to wielder's Intelligence modifier), the artifact begins to feed on the wielder.
The wielder looses one Hit Die daily for every day it has not been fed, after the aloted time.
These lost Hit Die cannot be used to heal during a short rest. If the Hit Die reach zero, the blade rejects the user and deems him unworthy to be his wielder, forcibly breaking their attunement bond.
The forced un-attunement deals 1d10 of psychic damage per wielder's level, and may never be attuned to Gloom again. 
Proficiency with a shortsword allows you to add your proficiency bonus to the attack roll for any attack you make with it.
